context: Discussion. We remark that the factor (1 − α)−1 scales polynomially with the mixing time τ , commonly used to bound regret in infinite-horizon settings (see Table 1). The T 3/4 dependency of MDPP-K comes from applying OMD over state-action distribution sequences initialized with varying distributions ρt per episode. Lower bounds for the√ adversarial infinite-horizon problem are known only in the case of known dynamics, yielding O( T ) in the full information setting (Chandrasekaran and Tewari, 2021). For unknown dynamics, establishing a lower bound remains an open problem. Regarding the dependence of the regret on the MDP parameters, it is known that exploration bonuses lead to an upper bound with an N 3 dependence (Luo et al., 2021), introducing an extra factor of N compared to the episodic RL lower bound. In our setting, we show that MDPP-K exhibits the same dependence. Concerning the dependence on the number of states, prior work (Moreno et al., 2025b) shows that, in episodic RL, combining exploration p bonuses with OMD in the occupancy-measure space yields a |X |3/2 dependence, an additional |X | over the lower bound arising from the constants in the bonus terms (see Eq. (7)). In our setting, OMD must additionally handle changing initial state distributions, and the exploration bonuses appearing in the constraints influence these variations. As a result, the same constant is incurred once more, leading to an overall |X |5/4 dependence. The computational complexity of MDPP-K increases linearly with |X |, |A|, and N , due to the structure of the closed-form output policy in Eq. (24). When we refer to the method as having low computational complexity, we mean that it admits a closed-form solution, as detailed in App. H, so no additional optimization step or external solver is required.
